<noinclude><pagequality level="1" user="Amire80" /></noinclude><section begin=par87 />{{GHGmargin-letter|87|d}}
The ending ''îm'' is also common in Phoenician, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=צדנם|translate=Sidonii}}; Assyrian has ''âni'' (acc. to P. Haupt originally ''âmi'', cf. {{GHGpar|88|d}}); Aramaic has ''în''; Arabic ''ûna'' (nominative) and ''îna'' (in the oblique cases, but in vulgar Arabic ''în'' is also used for the nominative); Ethiopic ''ân''. Cf. also the verbal ending {{GHGheb|text=וּן}} in the 3rd plur. perf. ({{GHGpar|44|l}}) and in the 3rd and 2nd plur. impf. ({{GHGpar|47|m}}).<ref>On the connexion between all these endings see Dietrich’s ''Abhandl. zur hebr. Gramm.'', Leipzig, 1846, p. 51 ff.; Halévy, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|REJ.|Revue des Études Juives. Paris, 1880 ff.}}}} 1888, p. 138 ff. [cf. also Driver, {{GHGcite|title=Tenses}}, § 6, Obs. 2].</ref>

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|e}}
Less frequent, or only apparent terminations of the plur. masc. are—

(''a'') {{GHGheb|text=־ִין}}, as in Aramaic,<ref>So also always in the Mêša‛ inscription, e.g. line 2 {{GHGheb|text=שלשן|translate=thirty}}; line 4 {{GHGheb|text=מלכן|translate=kings}}; line 5 {{GHGheb|text=ימן רבן|translate=many days}}, &c.</ref> found almost exclusively in the later books of the O.T. (apart from the poetical use in some of the older and even the oldest portions), viz. {{GHGheb|text=מְלָכִין|translate=kings}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Pr|chapter=31|verse=3}}, {{GHGheb|text=צִֽדֹנִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 K|chapter=11|verse=33}}, {{GHGheb|text=רָצִין|translate=the guard}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 K|chapter=11|verse=13}}, {{GHGheb|text=חִטִּין|translate=wheat}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=4|verse=9}}; defectively {{GHGheb|text=אִיִּן|translate=islands}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=26|verse=18}}; {{GHGheb|text=יָמִין|translate=days}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Dn|chapter=12|verse=13}}. Cf. also {{GHGheb|text=מִדִּין|translate=carpets}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=10}}, in the North-Palestinian song of Deborah, which also has other linguistic peculiarities; {{GHGheb|text=עִיִּין|translate=heaps}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Mi|chapter=3|verse=12}} (before {{GHGheb|text=ת}}; cf. {{GHGpar|44|k}}); {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּין|translate=words}} (from the really Aram. {{GHGheb|text=מִלָּה}}), {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=4|verse=2}}, and twelve other places in Job (beside {{GHGheb|text=מִלִּים}}, ten times in Job); further, {{GHGheb|text=חַיִּין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=24|verse=22}}, {{GHGheb|text=אֲחֵרִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jb|chapter=31|verse=10|hidebook=1}}, and {{GHGheb|text=שׁוֹמֵמִין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=1|verse=4}}, {{GHGheb|text=תַּנִּין}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=4|verse=3|hidebook=1}}.—The following forms are doubtful:

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|f}}
(''b'') {{GHGheb|text=־ִי}} (with the {{GHGheb|text=ם}} rejected, as, according to some, in the ''dual'' {{GHGheb|text=יָדַי}} for {{GHGheb|text=יָדַ֫יִם}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ez|chapter=13|verse=18}}, cf. {{GHGpar|88|c}}), e.g. {{GHGheb|text=מִנִּי|translate=stringed instruments}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=45|verse=9}} for {{GHGheb|text=מִנִּים}} (unless it is to be so written)<ref>According to some this ''î'' is simply due to a neglect of the point ({{GHGpar|5|m}}), which in MSS. and elsewhere marked the abbreviation of the plur. ending.</ref>; {{GHGheb|text=עַמִּי|translate=peoples}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=144|verse=2}}, and, probably, also {{GHGbible-ref|book=La|chapter=3|verse=14}} (in {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=22|verse=44}} it may be taken as {{GHGheb|text=עַמִּי|translate=my people}}; cf. in the parallel passage {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ps|chapter=18|verse=44}} {{GHGheb|text=עָם}}; also in {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ct|chapter=8|verse=2}} the ''î'' of {{GHGheb|text=רִמֹּנִי}} is better regarded as a ''suffix''); see also {{GHGbible-ref|book=2 S|chapter=23|verse=8}} as compared with {{GHGbible-ref|book=1 Ch|chapter=11|verse=11}}, and on the whole question Gesenius, {{GHGcite|title=Lehrgebäude}}, p. 524 ff. More doubtful still is—

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|g}}
(''c'') {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} (like the constr. state in Syriac), which is supposed to appear in e.g. {{GHGheb|text=שָׂרַי|translate=princes}}, {{GHGbible-ref|book=Ju|chapter=5|verse=15}} (perhaps ''my princes'' is intended: read either the constr. st. {{GHGheb|text=שָׂרֵי}}, which also has good authority, or with LXX {{GHGheb|text=שָׁרִים}}); for {{GHGheb|text=חַלּוֹנָ֔י וס׳}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Jer|chapter=22|verse=14}} (according to others ''dual'', see {{GHGpar|88|c}}, or a loan word, cf. {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZA.|Zeitschrift für Assyriologie und verwandte Gebiete, ed. by C. Bezold. Lpz. 18S6 ff.}}}} iii. 93) read {{GHGheb|text=חַלּוֹנָיו סָפוֹן}}. On {{GHGheb|text=גּוֹבַי}} and {{GHGheb|text=חוֹרַי}}, which have also been so explained, see above, {{GHGpar|86|i}}.—{{GHGheb|text=חֲשׂוּפַי}} {{GHGbible-ref|book=Is|chapter=20|verse=4}} (where the right reading is certainly {{GHGheb|text=חֲשׂוּפֵי}}) must be intended by the Masora either as a singular with the formative syllable {{GHGheb|text=־ַי}} =''bareness'' or, more probably, as a constr. st. with the original termination ''ay'' (cf. {{GHGpar|89|d}}) to avoid the harsh combination ''h<sup>a</sup>sûfê šēt''<ref>Prätorius, {{GHGcite|title={{abbr|ZDMG.|Zeitschrift der deutschen morgenländischen Gesellschaft, Lpz. 1846 ff., since 1903 ed. by A. Fischer.}}}} 1903, p. 525, regards {{GHGheb|text=הֲשׂוּפַי}} as an instance of the affix of endearment (cf. {{GHGheb|text=אֲחוּמַי}}, {{GHGheb|text=כְּלוּבַי}}) transferred to an appellative, but such an explanation is rendered unlikely by the meaning of this isolated instance.</ref>; in {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנָי|translate=the Lord}} (prop. ''my lord'', from the plur. ''majestatis'', {{GHGheb|text=אֲדֹנִים|translate=lord}}), the ''ay'' was originally a ''suffix'', {{GHGpar|135|q}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|h}}
(''d'') {{GHGheb|text=־ָם}} a supposed ''plural'' ending in {{GHGheb|text=כִּנָּם}}={{GHGheb|text=כִּנִּים|translate=gnats}} (or ''lice''), and {{GHGheb|text=סֻלָּם|translate=ladder}} (supposed by some to be a plur. like our ''stairs''); but cf. on the former, {{GHGpar|85|t}}.

{{GHGmargin-letter|87|i}}
'''2.''' The plural termination of the ''feminine gender'' is generally indicated by the termination {{GHGheb|text=וֹת}} (often written defectively {{GHGheb|text=־תֹ}}, e.g. {{GHGheb|text=תְּהִלָּה|translate=song of praise, psalm}}, plur. {{GHGheb|text=תְּהִלּוֹת}} (only in post-biblical Hebrew<section end=par87 /><noinclude>
